theory.overview: Quantum walks are the quantum analog of classical random walks, providing a framework for quantum algorithms with quadratically faster spread (σ ∝ t vs σ ∝ √t). Two models exist: discrete-time (DTQW) with coin operator and continuous-time (CTQW) under Hamiltonian evolution. Quantum walks enable faster search on graphs and solve element distinctness in O(N^{2/3}) queries.

sections.title: Discrete-Time Quantum Walk
sections.content: DTQW uses position and coin Hilbert spaces. State: |ψ⟩ = Σ_x (a_x|x⟩|→⟩ + b_x|x⟩|←⟩). Each step applies coin then shift: U = S·(C ⊗ I). Hadamard coin creates superposition. Spreads ballistically with σ ∝ t.

sections.title: Quantum Walk Search
sections.content: Quantum walks search marked vertices faster than classical. On complete graph: O(√N) vs classical O(N). Oracle modifies walk at marked vertices. Works on structured graphs where database isn't fully connected.

sections.title: Element Distinctness
sections.content: Ambainis's quantum walk algorithm finds collisions in O(N^{2/3}) queries, optimal for quantum. Walks on Johnson graph J(N, r) of subsets. Applications: collision finding, triangle finding, formula evaluation.

import numpy as np
# Discrete-time quantum walk simulation
def quantum_walk_step(state, coin, shift):
    n = len(state) // 2
    new_state = np.zeros_like(state)
    for x in range(n):
        new_state[2*x:2*x+2] = coin @ state[2*x:2*x+2]
    return shift @ new_state

# Hadamard coin
